$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**

derivations.claim: For $N\ge2$, index each binary factor's ordered basis by $\{0,1\}$; a string $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$ has even parity when $\sum_jx_j$ is even. Let $\pi_N$ be the diagonal matrix with entry $2^{-(N-1)}$ on even strings and zero on odd strings, and let $\gamma_N=I/2^N$. There are $2^{N-1}$ even strings: the first $N-1$ bits can be arbitrary and the last bit is uniquely determined. Thus both matrices are nonnegative of trace one. Fix $0\le k<N$ coordinates and their values. Among the $N-k\ge1$ unassigned coordinates, exactly half of the $2^{N-k}$ completions have the required parity, namely $2^{N-k-1}$. Summing by [F1], the marginal diagonal entry of each fixed $k$-bit string is $2^{N-k-1}/2^{N-1}=2^{-k}$; all off-diagonal entries vanish. Thus $(\pi_N)_k=I/2^k=(\gamma_N)_k$ for every proper block.

On an even string the diagonal difference $\pi_N-\gamma_N$ is $2^{-(N-1)}-2^{-N}=2^{-N}$; on an odd string it is $-2^{-N}$. There are $2^N$ strings in total, so the absolute eigenvalues sum to $2^N2^{-N}=1$. Therefore $\|\pi_N-\gamma_N\|_1=1$ for every $N$.

Let $P_{\rm even}$ be the diagonal matrix with entry one on even strings and zero on odd strings. Both $P_{\rm even}$ and $I-P_{\rm even}$ are nonnegative and sum to $I$, so they form a two-outcome POVM by [F2]. Their first-effect trace pairings are $\operatorname{Tr}(\pi_NP_{\rm even})=1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma_NP_{\rm even})=1/2$, a gap of $1/2$. Hence equality of all proper local marginals does not entail global trace-norm convergence or equality of global POVM trace pairings. This is a mathematical separation; no physical probability interpretation is adopted.
